papers.summary: Defines a behavioral compression rate for LoRA adapters and shows that compressibility depends on the dataset–base-model pair. In a corrupted-data control, adapters trained at higher rank recovered more accuracy after compression to the same rank-1, one-bit endpoint.
papers.relevance: Directly informs whether training choices can improve low-rank compressibility while preserving behavior. The experiments concern adapters, not full-model pretraining.

evidence.quote: Each adapter is trained once and then compressed over a range of operating points, without retraining.
final GSM8K accuracy rises from approximately 60% when trained at rank 1 to approximately 78–81% when trained at ranks 2–16.

papers.title: The Behavioral Rate of Fine-Tuning: Compression as a Measure of Useful Information

papers.summary: Tracks LoRA singular spectra and subspaces during SFT and RL on mathematical reasoning tasks. Controlled SFT–RL interpolation identifies group-mean baseline subtraction as a source of the contrasting dynamics, motivating stage-specific spectral updates.
papers.relevance: A direct match to the researcher’s questions about optimization, effective rank, and singular-value spectra in LoRA.

both contrasts appear only once a group-mean baseline is subtracted from the reward

papers.title: Spectral and Subspace Dynamics of LoRA in Supervised Fine-Tuning and Reinforcement Learning

papers.summary: Develops tangent–normal geometry for adaptive LoRA rank expansion. On LLaMA3-8B, it reports a higher average commonsense score with fewer trainable parameters, although its retrieved runtime and peak-memory comparison is on a vision task.
papers.relevance: Addresses principled rank selection and optimization outside the current LoRA subspace.

evidence.quote: On LLaMA3-8B, it raises the average commonsense score from 86.61 to 88.45 while reducing trainable parameters from 42.0M to 14.4M.

papers.summary: ResQAdam retains a signed residual outside a low-rank optimizer subspace for quantization-aware LLM training. Against AdamW on three LLMs, reported optimizer-state memory falls by about 71–73%, total peak memory by 15–20%, and throughput by less than 2%.
papers.relevance: Directly addresses the quality, memory, and throughput tradeoff of low-rank optimizer-state compression, including a failure mode of GaLore and LDAdam in QAT.

papers.summary: Compares Muon and AdamW across OLMo-style pretraining scales and downstream fine-tuning. Muon achieves lower pretraining loss, but AdamW has a better learning–forgetting tradeoff after sufficiently large data budgets, with the crossover shifting as model size grows.
papers.relevance: Tests whether an optimizer’s pretraining advantage survives fine-tuning and how that tradeoff changes with scale.

evidence.quote: we pretrain OLMo-style 30M–600M models ( Groeneveld et al., 2024 ; Team OLMo et al., 2025 ) on 150 150 M to 154 154 B DCLM tokens
On every dataset Muon is better than or level with AdamW below the crossover and AdamW is better beyond it.

papers.title: Pretraining Data Scale Reverses the Muon-AdamW Fine-Tuning Gap

papers.summary: In a quadratic-network matrix-factorization model, proves that finite Newton–Schulz depth can change early rank selection and, under an additional condition, bypass the first stationary point reached by gradient flow.
papers.relevance: A focused theoretical contribution to the researcher’s Muon, Newton–Schulz, and effective-rank interests; applicability to LLM training remains open.

evidence.quote: We show that the number of Newton–Schulz steps can change the rank selected during the early stages of training
An immediate open question is whether similar dynamical descriptions can be established for more general models and under weaker assumptions.

papers.title: Finite Spectral Depth Controls Gaussian Entrance Rank and Avoidance of the First Gradient-Flow Saddle

papers.summary: CORE combines passage retrieval, snippet selection, source expansion, and duplicate suppression in a training-free deep-research harness. In controlled closed-search comparisons, it reports higher answer accuracy and evidence recall than two harness baselines across three agent models and benchmarks.
papers.relevance: Directly applicable to the user’s handwritten research-digest harness and its evidence/context-management design.

evidence.quote: CORE’s context manager lets the agent expand the context around previously retrieved sources and deduplicates snippets across searches.
Across three agent models, CORE achieves the highest accuracy and evidence recall in every model–benchmark comparison

papers.title: CORE: Coarse-to-Fine Search with Context Management for Deep Research
